q: Is the '2 genomic islands' claim (GI-I 25.3 kb / GI-II 70.6 kb) a real biological signal or an IslandViewer-4 tuning artifact, and how many HGT islands does 2NE11 really carry?
basis: REPORT.md §4.5 records a real discrepancy: the paper's IslandViewer-4 (SIGI-HMM + IslandPath-DIMOB + IslandPick consensus) reports exactly 2 islands, while our independent DIMOB-style single-method predictor finds 7 mobility-associated atypical-composition regions (largest ~48 kb / 51 genes) including a T4SS/conjugative cluster at ~4.03–4.07 Mb. The paper's Fig. 2 numbers may reflect specific consensus cutoffs, not a ground-truth count. This matters biologically because HGT/T4SS islands are the likely vehicles for the metal-resistance and dye-tolerance cassettes that motivate the bioremediation thesis.
next_steps: Submit GCF_014263185.1 to the actual IslandViewer 4 web service (or run the offline pipeline) and diff against our 7-island DIMOB output.
Run mobileOG-db / MobileElementFinder / PlasmidFinder on the assembly to build a curated MGE catalogue independent of composition-bias methods.
For each candidate island, BLAST the flanking regions against closely related Shewanella algae genomes (e.g. MARS 14, OK-1) to confirm HGT origin via presence/absence in sister taxa.
Cross-reference island coordinates with the metal-resistance and Mtr loci to test whether the bioremediation-relevant genes actually sit inside HGT islands.

q: Is the paper's 'OmcA duplication' claim (three adjacent decaheme cytochromes at HU689_RS08370/75/80) a genuine gene duplication event, or the standard Shewanella MtrC+OmcA pair mislabeled as two OmcAs by product-string annotation drift?
basis: REPORT.md §4.3 confirms three adjacent OmcA/MtrC decaheme cytochromes were found in the RefSeq annotation but explicitly flags in the Genuine Critique that we did not check whether this is a true duplication or the canonical MtrC + OmcA architecture that Shewanella spp. carry by default. Since OmcA and MtrC are paralogs with high sequence similarity, RefSeq product strings can flip between them; the paper's 'duplication' claim (which motivates enhanced extracellular electron transfer as a decolorization mechanism) may not survive careful ortholog assignment.
next_steps: Extract the three candidate decaheme cytochrome protein sequences and run reciprocal BLAST vs S. oneidensis MR-1 OmcA (SO_1779) and MtrC (SO_1778) reference proteins to assign orthology.
Build a phylogenetic tree of decaheme cytochromes across sequenced Shewanella spp. to see whether the third gene clusters with OmcA (=duplication) or forms its own clade (=novel paralog).
Check synteny of the mtrCAB / omcA cluster in S. algae MARS 14, OK-1, and related strains: is the '3rd cytochrome' present in all S. algae or unique to 2NE11?
If duplication is confirmed, test whether the two OmcA copies are under different selective pressure (dN/dS) or expressed under different conditions (would need RNA-seq).

q: Can the 197-aa FMN-dependent NADH-azoreductase (HU689_RS20690) alone account for the reported 89–97% decolorization of azo/anthraquinone dyes in 12 h, or does the phenotype require the Mtr extracellular electron transfer pathway and/or the Dyp peroxidase acting in concert?
basis: REPORT.md §4.3 confirms byte-for-byte the paper's azoreductase (594 bp, 197 aa) and Dyp peroxidase (936 bp, 311 aa), and confirms the Mtr operon + OmcA cluster. But the paper only asserts that these genes exist — it does not test which enzyme actually does the decolorization work in vivo, or whether anthraquinone dyes (structurally distinct from azo dyes) require the peroxidase rather than the azoreductase. The 89–97% rate is high enough that a single 197-aa monomeric azoreductase probably cannot explain it alone.
next_steps: Homology-model the 197-aa azoreductase against solved azoreductase structures (e.g. E. coli AzoR, PDB 2HPV) and dock representative azo dyes to estimate kcat/Km and turnover feasibility.

Compare 2NE11's azoreductase copy number and sequence to Shewanella strains with known decolorization rates from the literature (e.g. S. decolorationis S12) to see whether 2NE11 is enzymatically unusual.
Design a transcriptomics experiment (RNA-seq ± dye exposure) to identify which of azoreductase / Dyp peroxidase / Mtr pathway genes are induced by azo vs anthraquinone dye challenge.
Attempt heterologous expression of HU689_RS20690 in E. coli BL21 and measure decolorization activity vs a panel of dyes to establish the enzyme's intrinsic substrate range.

q: Do the metal-resistance (cadA, corA/C, zntB, arsA/B/C) and CRISPR-Cas (Type I-F) cassettes sit inside the T4SS/conjugative HGT islands identified at ~4.03–4.07 Mb, making 2NE11's industrial-effluent adaptation a mobilizable trait — or are they core-genome loci shared with all S. algae?
basis: REPORT.md §4.4 and §4.5 confirm both the metal-resistance cassette and the CRISPR-Cas system are present, and independently confirm a T4SS/conjugative machinery cluster at ~4.03–4.07 Mb. But we did not test whether the resistance/CRISPR loci are physically linked to the mobilizable region. This is a load-bearing biological question for the bioremediation-agent thesis: transferable resistance genes have very different deployment implications than core-genome ones, and Type I-F CRISPR arrays can prevent uptake of the very plasmids/phages that carry metal-resistance cassettes.
next_steps: Map RefSeq coordinates of cadA, corA/C, zntB, arsA/B/C, and the Type I-F CRISPR array against our 7 predicted GI coordinates and against the paper's 2 GIs — record overlap fractions.

For each CRISPR spacer in the array, BLAST vs a curated Shewanella phage + plasmid database to reconstruct 2NE11's recent uptake/immunity history and check whether spacers target elements carrying similar resistance genes.
Compare gene neighborhoods of the metal-resistance loci in 2NE11 vs core-genome S. algae strains (e.g. MARS 14, OK-1) to detect insertions/inversions consistent with HGT acquisition.
Test for co-localization with tRNA genes, integrases, and other classic HGT signatures at the boundaries of the resistance loci.

q: Are the small annotation-drift differences observed between the paper's 2020/2022 PGAP (4,288 protein-coding, 4,334 CDS, 46 pseudo) and our 2026 re-annotation (4,295 protein-coding, 4,343 CDS, 48 pseudo) biologically meaningful — e.g. do the 7 newly-called CDSs land in ecologically interesting regions (islands, cytochromes, azo/peroxidase families) — or are they uniformly distributed noise?
basis: REPORT.md §4.1 documents a +7 protein-coding, +9 CDS, +2 pseudogene delta between the paper's original PGAP and NCBI's 2026-04-02 re-annotation, and shrugs this off as 'annotation drift' within 0.2%. But small deltas can be biologically loaded: a new call inside the Mtr operon, a split/merged azoreductase, or a newly-recognized pseudogene in a CRISPR-cas gene would each be individually publishable. We did not check where the deltas actually fall.
next_steps: Diff the 2020/2022 PGAP GFF against the 2026-04-02 re-annotated GFF to enumerate exactly which locus tags were added, removed, split, merged, or reclassified as pseudogenes.
Intersect the diff coordinates with our GI predictions, the Mtr operon coordinates, and the decolorization-gene coordinates to test for enrichment in ecologically interesting regions.
For each newly-called or newly-pseudogenized gene, run manual protein-domain analysis (Pfam / InterProScan) to check function assignment.
Report whether any of the paper's specific claims (locus-tag-level) are affected by the re-annotation, e.g. whether HU689_04585/04700/21345 still exist as annotated CDSs in the 2026 version.
